summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted one day after discharge due to an episode of diaphoresis, lightheadedness, and a brief fluttering sensation in the neck while walking. He had been recently treated for decompensated systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and multifocal pneumonia. Workup revealed no pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac injury, with stable vital signs and improving lung findings on imaging. Possible causes included orthostasis from recent diuresis, transient hypoglycemia, or a brief episode of atrial fibrillation with rapid rate. His home metoprolol dose was lower than hospital dose due to insurance restrictions. He received methadone during admission and was clinically stable the following morning but eloped before completing discharge planning.
